_what_this_is: The numbers the documents publish that had to be *measured* rather than counted.
A count is derived from the tree at check time and never stored: the unit suite
count is the RUN_TEST list in tests/test_suite.cpp, and the corpus totals are the
cases in tests/js-conformance and tests/dom-conformance, parsed by the same parser
the runners use. A score is measured by running something, so it is written down
here with the command that produced it and the day it was produced.
tools/ci/check_numbers.py reads this file. Its check mode fails when a figure in
the documents disagrees with the ledger or with the tree; its --write mode
rewrites the figures the documents publish from both, in one pass. `make metrics`
is --write, and is what to run after merging main instead of editing the counts
A figure here is not a promise: it is what a command printed on the date beside
it. When the command no longer prints it, re-run the command, not the number.
Not in this ledger, and why: the XML score needs a corpus that is downloaded
on first use (tests/xml/README.md), so `make xml-conformance` is the authority
for it and XML_FLOOR stays in the Makefile by hand. The two ASan floors are the
same scores under sanitizers and are written by `make asan`, not here.
